newsitem.title: BRAZIL: TENNIS-AUSTRIA DROPS DAVIS CUP DOUBLES AS MUSTER STORMS OFF COURT.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-AUSTRIA DROPS DAVIS CUP DOUBLES AS MUSTER STORMS OFF COURT.

text.p: Temperamental Austrian tennis star Thomas Muster cost his country a crucial point in its Davis Cup World Group qualifying tie with Brazil by storming off the court in the fifth set of Saturday's doubles match.
The world number three abandoned the pivotal match in protest at what he claimed was bad crowd behaviour to give Brazil a 2-1 lead heading into Sunday's reverse singles.

Brazil's Jaime Oncins and Gustavo Kuerten were leading Muster and Udo Plamberger 2-0 in the final set when Muster lost his cool. The Brazilians had won the first and third sets and the match ended prematurely with the score 7-6, 4-6, 6-3, 3-6, 2-0, 30-15.

Witnesses said Muster, who always seems to have a gripe about something, refused to carry on because he was angry at the umpire's refusal to act over noise in the crowd while the Austrians were serving.
Muster claimed several times that he could hear people in the crowd calling out his name as he served, but the chair umpire said he could not hear anything.
When numerous protests by the cranky Austrian produced no satisfaction from officials, Muster stormed off court amid jeers, angrily pointing his finger at someone in the crowd.
Muster had also moaned several times during the match about what he said was a small bump in the court surface.
It was not known whether he would take part in Sunday's reverse singles, but Saturday's fit of pique could help propel Brazil back into the elite World Group after a three-year absence.
